# Pokédex

A Pokédex app on live data from PokeAPI. Specs are in `specs/`.

- Expo Router, TanStack Query, expo-sqlite. Must run in Expo Go.
- Screens in `src/app/`, data through hooks in `src/hooks/`, API and SQL in `src/services/`.
- Colours, type colours and spacing in `src/constants/theme.ts`. Font: Rubik with Expo Font.
- Shared setup (API client, query client, database): reuse what is listed here, never add a second one. When you set up something new that other features will use, add a line here: what it is and where it lives.
- Before you write code for an issue: post a plan (which files, how, what you are unsure about) and a `- [ ]` task list as one comment on the issue with `gh issue comment`. Wait for my go. Tick off tasks with `gh issue comment --edit-last` while you build.
- After building: run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx expo lint`. Both must pass.
- No new dependencies without asking me first.

---

This is an Expo/React Native mobile application. Prioritize mobile-first patterns, performance, and cross-platform compatibility.

## Expo has changed — do not trust your training data

Expo ships breaking changes every SDK release. APIs you remember are likely renamed, moved, or removed. Before writing any code that touches an Expo, EAS, or React Native API:

1. Read the major version of the `expo` package in `package.json`.
2. Fetch the matching versioned docs: `https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v<major>.0.0/`
3. For anything else, fetch https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt — an index of all Expo docs with corrections to common LLM misconceptions. Follow its links to the specific page you need; never answer from memory.

## Commands

Use `bunx` instead of `npx` if the project uses bun (`bun.lock` present).

```bash
npx expo install <package>  # ALWAYS use instead of npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add — resolves SDK-compatible versions
npx expo start              # start the dev server
npx expo lint               # lint
npx tsc --noEmit            # typecheck
npx expo-doctor             # diagnose dependency and config issues
npx expo install --fix      # fix incompatible package versions
```

Run lint and typecheck before declaring any task done.

## Navigation & Routing

- Use **Expo Router** for all navigation. Routes live in `src/app/` — every file there is a screen, `_layout.tsx` files define navigators. Keep non-route code (components, hooks, utils) outside `src/app/`.
- Import `Link`, `router`, and `useLocalSearchParams` from `expo-router`.
- Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/router/introduction.md

## Building with EAS

Use EAS to build, sign, and submit the app in the cloud (`eas build`, `eas submit`) and to ship over-the-air updates (`eas update`) — no local Xcode or Android Studio required. Run EAS CLI as `bunx eas-cli <command>` in Bun projects, or `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` otherwise; substitute that for bare `eas` in docs examples.
Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/index.md

## Rules

- If `ios/` and `android/` directories do not exist, they are generated (Continuous Native Generation). Never create or edit them by hand — configure native behavior in `app.json` and config plugins.
- Expo Go only includes its bundled native modules. After adding a library with native code, the app needs a development build: `npx expo run:ios|android` locally, or `eas build --profile development`.
- Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries, and check your available skills before adding dependencies. Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/index.md

file.content:
# Pokédex

A Pokédex app for Pokémon fans. You can scroll through all Pokémon, search
by name, open a Pokémon to see its details and evolutions, keep your
favorites, and compare two Pokémon side by side. All data comes live from
PokeAPI. The design follows the course Figma file.

## Core action

Find a Pokémon and see what it can do.

## Features

1. [List](./features/list.md): all Pokémon in a list, live from the API.
2. [Search](./features/search.md): find any Pokémon by part of its name.
3. [Detail](./features/detail.md): about, stats and evolution chain of one Pokémon.
4. [Favorites](./features/favorites.md): save Pokémon, still there after a restart.
5. [Compare](./features/compare.md): two Pokémon side by side, per stat who is stronger.

## Data

- **API**: [PokeAPI](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2). Public, no key, no login.
- **Endpoints**:
  - `/pokemon?limit=...&offset=...`: names and URLs for the list and search.
  - `/pokemon/{id}`: number, artwork, types, stats, height, weight.
  - `/pokemon-species/{id}`: description text and the link to the evolution chain.
  - `/evolution-chain/{id}`: the evolution chain.
- **Stored on the phone**: table `favorites` in SQLite: `id`, `name`, `created_at`.

## Technical choices

- **Stored in SQLite**: the favorites (id, name, date added), not the
  Pokémon data itself, because PokeAPI is the source of truth and TanStack
  Query already caches it. SQLite, not AsyncStorage, because I sort favorites
  by date added and need a quick "is this a favorite?" check by `id`.
- **Native feature**: haptics (`expo-haptics`) when you tap the favorite
  button on the detail screen, so you feel that it worked. The alternative
  was Share, but a favorite tap is the action people do most.

## Technical core

- [ ] Runs in Expo Go
- [ ] Live data through TanStack Query
- [ ] At least 2 screens with Expo Router
- [ ] Something in SQLite that survives a restart
- [ ] Loading and error state on every load
- [ ] One native feature: haptics, on the favorite button (detail screen)
- [ ] TypeScript and ESLint without errors
- [ ] UI, data and logic in separate files

## Optional

- [ ] Clean TypeScript: no `any`, no `as` casts, no `@ts-ignore`
- [ ] Design: pixel perfect, as in the Figma file
- [ ] No warnings: no `console.log`, none in the terminal or on screen

## Out of scope

- Accounts or sync between phones.
- Moves, abilities, items, locations.
- Battles.
- A web version.

# List

## Goal

See all Pokémon in one list, so I can browse them and open one.

## Constraints

- Home screen: `src/app/index.tsx`.
- Data from PokeAPI `/pokemon` through TanStack Query, in a hook in `src/hooks/` and a service in `src/services/`.
- Number and artwork come from the id in the URL. No extra request per row.
- Rows as in the Figma design: artwork, number, name. Font Rubik with Expo Font, colours from `src/constants/theme.ts`.
- `FlatList`, so long lists scroll smoothly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The list shows all ~1300 Pokémon, with artwork, number and name.
- [ ] Scrolling stays smooth, also at the end of the list.
- [ ] A loading state while the list loads.
- [ ] An error with a Retry button when the request fails.
- [ ] Tapping a row opens the detail screen of that Pokémon.

## Out of Scope

- Types or stats in the rows.
- Sorting or filters.

gh issue comment 1 --body "## Plan for Issue #1: List Feature Setup

### Overview
This issue sets up the foundational infrastructure for the Pokédex app and implements the list feature. I'll create the shared services, configure the theme, set up fonts, and build the Pokémon list with proper data fetching.

### Files to Create/Modify

**New Files:**
- \`src/constants/theme.ts\` - Color palette (#DC0A2D primary), spacing, type colors
- \`src/services/api.ts\` - API client for PokeAPI with base configuration
- \`src/services/queryClient.ts\` - TanStack Query client setup
- \`src/hooks/usePokemonList.ts\` - Hook for fetching Pokémon list data
- \`src/services/pokemon.ts\` - API service functions for Pokémon endpoints
- \`src/components/PokemonRow.tsx\` - Reusable list row component (artwork, number, name)
- \`src/app/pokemon/[id].tsx\` - Placeholder detail screen
- \`src/app/_layout.tsx\` - Update to add QueryClientProvider and font loading

**Modified Files:**
- \`src/app/index.tsx\` - Implement the Pokémon list with FlatList
- \`AGENTS.md\` - Document all shared setup components

### Architecture Decisions

1. **API Client**: Axios-like fetch wrapper with base URL (https://pokeapi.co/api/v2)

# Pokédex

A Pokédex app on live data from PokeAPI. Specs are in `specs/`.

- Expo Router, TanStack Query, expo-sqlite. Must run in Expo Go.
- Screens in `src/app/`, data through hooks in `src/hooks/`, API and SQL in `src/services/`.
- Colours, type colours and spacing in `src/constants/theme.ts`. Font: Rubik with Expo Font.
- Shared setup (API client, query client, database): reuse what is listed here, never add a second one. When you set up something new that other features will use, add a line here: what it is and where it lives.
- Before you write code for an issue: post a plan (which files, how, what you are unsure about) and a `- [ ]` task list as one comment on the issue with `gh issue comment`. Wait for my go. Tick off tasks with `gh issue comment --edit-last` while you build.
- After building: run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx expo lint`. Both must pass.
- No new dependencies without asking me first.

---

This is an Expo/React Native mobile application. Prioritize mobile-first patterns, performance, and cross-platform compatibility.

## Expo has changed — do not trust your training data

Expo ships breaking changes every SDK release. APIs you remember are likely renamed, moved, or removed. Before writing any code that touches an Expo, EAS, or React Native API:

1. Read the major version of the `expo` package in `package.json`.
2. Fetch the matching versioned docs: `https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v<major>.0.0/`
3. For anything else, fetch https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt — an index of all Expo docs with corrections to common LLM misconceptions. Follow its links to the specific page you need; never answer from memory.

## Commands

Use `bunx` instead of `npx` if the project uses bun (`bun.lock` present).

```bash
npx expo install <package>  # ALWAYS use instead of npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add — resolves SDK-compatible versions
npx expo start              # start the dev server
npx expo lint               # lint
npx tsc --noEmit            # typecheck
npx expo-doctor             # diagnose dependency and config issues
npx expo install --fix      # fix incompatible package versions
```

Run lint and typecheck before declaring any task done.

## Navigation & Routing

- Use **Expo Router** for all navigation. Routes live in `src/app/` — every file there is a screen, `_layout.tsx` files define navigators. Keep non-route code (components, hooks, utils) outside `src/app/`.
- Import `Link`, `router`, and `useLocalSearchParams` from `expo-router`.
- Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/router/introduction.md

## Building with EAS

Use EAS to build, sign, and submit the app in the cloud (`eas build`, `eas submit`) and to ship over-the-air updates (`eas update`) — no local Xcode or Android Studio required. Run EAS CLI as `bunx eas-cli <command>` in Bun projects, or `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` otherwise; substitute that for bare `eas` in docs examples.
Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/index.md

## Rules

- If `ios/` and `android/` directories do not exist, they are generated (Continuous Native Generation). Never create or edit them by hand — configure native behavior in `app.json` and config plugins.
- Expo Go only includes its bundled native modules. After adding a library with native code, the app needs a development build: `npx expo run:ios|android` locally, or `eas build --profile development`.
- Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries, and check your available skills before adding dependencies. Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/index.md
